thinking: First round, nothing measured yet. Key algebraic reading: for symmetric f, max(f*f)=||f||_2^2, so R=||f*f||_2^2/(||f||_1^2||f||_2^2); equivalently R=(∫u^2)/(∫u) with u=(f*f)/max, so R measures how flat/rectangle-like f*f is. Box gives triangular f*f → 2/3 (p0001 confirms). A Gaussian bumps this to 1/√2≈0.707. Sparse delta-combs likely give (2-1/k)/3≤2/3, i.e. worse. So the real lever is a smooth single bump plus direct height optimization. I will put a general randomized height-improver in the deepen slot starting from a Gaussian seed, and use the two explores to scan parametric bump families to learn which shape is extremal.
gist: Round 1: interpret R as flatness of f*f; schedule a general height-improver seeded by a Gaussian (deepen) and two parametric bump-family scans (explore).

exps.change: Implement a general improver: if start is None or nearly flat, seed h = exp(-((linspace(-1,1,N=300))/0.33)^2), else h=start.copy(). thinking: Direct height optimization is the dominant lever (0.8078). Two structural clues: every high scorer has an ASYMMETRIC f*f peak (max at 0.324 and 0.562 of support), and flat-top profiles (p0005) beat the Gaussian. Mechanism: by Cauchy-Schwarz max(f*f)=||f||_2^2 only for symmetric f; an asymmetric f lowers ||f*f||_inf while keeping the bulk, which raises R. So the target is an asymmetric, flat-topped f whose f*f is as rectangle-like as possible. This round: (1) a real gradient optimizer (L-BFGS-B) on the p0004 line, (2) an explicit peak-suppression/asymmetry-tilt experiment on p0004, (3) develop the flat-top line from p0005 with direct optimization.
